title: Magnetic Forces & Fields
summary: A magnetic field exerts a force on moving charge, $F = qvB\sin\theta$, and on a current-carrying wire, $F = BIL\sin\theta$. The force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so charges move in circles of radius $r = mv/(qB)$, and current loops feel a torque $\tau = NBIA\sin\theta$. (University Physics Vol. 2, Ch. 11.)

concept_sections.heading: Force on a moving charge
concept_sections.explanation: A magnetic field $B$ pushes on charge only when it moves: $F = qvB\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the velocity and the field. A charge moving along the field ($\theta = 0$) feels no force; moving across it ($\theta = 90^\circ$) feels the maximum.

concept_sections.heading: Direction: the right-hand rule
concept_sections.explanation: The force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field, given by $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$. Point your right hand's fingers along $\vec{v}$, curl toward $\vec{B}$; the thumb gives the force on a positive charge (reverse it for negative). This is why the force never speeds a charge up — only turns it.

concept_sections.heading: Force on a current-carrying wire
concept_sections.explanation: A wire is just moving charges, so a field pushes on it too: $F = BIL\sin\theta$, where $I$ is the current, $L$ the length in the field, and $\theta$ the angle between the wire and $\vec{B}$. This force is what spins every electric motor.

concept_sections.heading: Circular motion
concept_sections.explanation: Because the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity, a charge entering a uniform field moves in a circle. Setting $qvB = mv^2/r$ gives radius $r = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$ and period $T = \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ (independent of speed) — the principle of cyclotrons and mass spectrometers.

concept_sections.heading: Torque on a current loop
concept_sections.explanation: A loop of $N$ turns carrying current $I$ with area $A$ in a field feels a torque $\tau = NBIA\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is between the field and the loop's normal. The loop twists to align — the working principle of motors and analog meters. The product $NIA$ is the loop's magnetic moment.

real_world_examples.title: Mass spectrometer
real_world_examples.scenario: A lab identifies molecules by their mass.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Ions of the same speed curve with radius $r = mv/(qB)$; heavier ions curve less. Measuring $r$ reveals the mass, separating the sample by molecular weight.

real_world_examples.title: Electric motor
real_world_examples.scenario: A motor turns electrical energy into rotation.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Current loops in a field feel torque $\tau = NBIA\sin\theta$. Commutators flip the current each half-turn so the torque keeps the shaft spinning one way.

real_world_examples.title: The aurora
real_world_examples.scenario: Charged particles from the Sun glow near the poles.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Earth's magnetic field bends the particles via $F = qvB\sin\theta$, funneling them along field lines toward the poles where they strike the atmosphere and glow.

problems.prompt: A charge $q = 1.6\times10^{-19}$ C moves at $v = 1.0\times10^{6}$ m/s perpendicular to a field $B = 0.50$ T. Find the force.
A wire of length $0.50$ m carries $3.0$ A perpendicular to a field $B = 0.20$ T. Find the force on it.
A positive charge moves in $+x$; the field points in $+y$. Which way is the magnetic force?
An electron ($m = 9.11\times10^{-31}$ kg) moves at $v = 1.0\times10^{7}$ m/s across a field $B = 0.010$ T. Find the radius of its circular path.
A proton moves at $v = 2.0\times10^{6}$ m/s perpendicular to $B = 0.30$ T. Find the force ($q = 1.6\times10^{-19}$ C).
In a velocity selector, $E = 1.0\times10^{4}$ V/m and $B = 0.020$ T are crossed. What speed passes straight through?
problems.hint: The electric and magnetic forces cancel when $v = E/B$.

problems.prompt: A wire carries $5.0$ A over a length $2.0$ m in a field $B = 0.40$ T at $30^\circ$ to the wire. Find the force.
Find the period of a proton's circular motion in $B = 0.50$ T ($m = 1.67\times10^{-27}$ kg, $q = 1.6\times10^{-19}$ C).
problems.hint: The period is independent of speed: $T = 2\pi m/(qB)$.

problems.prompt: A coil of $100$ turns, area $0.010\ \text{m}^2$, carries $2.0$ A in a field $B = 0.20$ T with the field in the plane of the loop. Find the torque.
solution_steps: Field in the plane means $\theta = 90^\circ$, so $\tau = NBIA$.

problems.prompt: How much work does the magnetic force do on a charge moving through a magnetic field, and why?
solution_steps: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity.
Work $= \vec{F}\cdot\vec{d}$, and a perpendicular force does no work.
So the magnetic force does zero work — it changes direction, not speed.
problems.hint: Think about the angle between the force and the motion.
